From: Tom Garner <tom.garner@lendwise.com>
To: mateo_alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T09:14:00-04:00
Subject: London pilot — small-footprint dedicated pool and SOW

Hi Mateo,

Quick intro — I'm Tom Garner, Head of Platform at Lendwise. We're preparing a demo and pilot that must run from the UK (data residency + latency guarantees) for a banking customer. We're exploring a small dedicated pool in London for a 3-month pilot with the option to convert to Dedicated after a successful trial.

Key constraints:
- Data must remain in the UK region (no cross-border processing).
- Target p95 latency for single-turn generation < 40 ms for typical prompts (~512 tokens).
- Expected steady-state: ~30 QPS of small-generation calls, with peak bursts to ~120 QPS for short windows (10-20 min).
- Token mix: mostly short generations (~60-200 tokens); occasional 1k+ for batch jobs (non-real-time).
- Compliance: customer will require SOC2 report and basic KMS integration.

What we need from Redwood:
1) A short SOW draft for a London pilot (timeline, deliverables, SLA during pilot).
2) Recommended pool sizing and suggested node configuration (we're comfortable with lightweight nodes; cost sensitive).
3) Any constraints on start date — we're targeting an in-region pilot starting the week of 2028-08-05.

If you can send a SOW and a sizing estimate, we can route internally for procurement and security checks. Happy to jump on a 30-min call this week to walk through requirements — Priya Sen (cc) will coordinate.

Thanks,
Tom

--
Tom Garner
Head of Platform, Lendwise
Tom.garner@lendwise.com

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Garner <tom.garner@lendwise.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-05-30T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: London pilot — small-footprint dedicated pool and SOW

Thanks Tom — appreciate the clear constraints. Looping in Laura (platform engineering) and Irene (capacity planning) to validate sizing and runbook items; Connor and Karthik on the commercial/contract side.

High level feasibility: this is doable as a London-region (eu-west-2) small-footprint Dedicated pilot. Based on the traffic profile you shared, initial recommendation is a 2-tier pilot configuration:

Option A (cost-conservative, will absorb short bursts with modest queuing):
- 4x inference nodes (each with 2x GPUs equivalent capacity) across 2 AZs (2 nodes per AZ)
- Autoscaling policy: scale up +1 node on sustained 60s CPU/GPU utilization > 70% (burst headroom retained)
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~30 QPS for small gens; burst coverage up to ~90-120 QPS with ~10-15s queuing on the high end
- Typical hourly cost: (ballpark) lower than mid-tier option; we'll provide ranges in the SOW

Option B (latency-optimized, higher cost):
- 6x inference nodes (3 per AZ) with higher memory profiles for KV cache and 1k+ token batch jobs
- Designed to hold p95 < 40 ms at target steady-state and tighter burst headroom

Notes and questions for sizing accuracy:
1) For the batch 1k+ token jobs, are those acceptable to schedule on lower-priority nodes or must they be real-time?
2) Do you expect simultaneous long-running streams or mostly single-turn calls?
3) Access to KMS for key wrapping in-region — do you have a preferred KMS provider in the UK?

Next steps I've attached a draft SOW (london-pilot-sow-draft.docx) and a quick pool-sizing workbook (pool-sizing-calculation.xlsx) with assumptions. Irene, can you confirm any procurement or capacity gating for a London onramp in August? Laura, will need an engineering estimate for the rollout and an ops runbook for failover to an EU fallback lane (data residency constraint noted).

If that looks OK, propose a 30-min sync: Thu 2028-05-31 10:00 BST / 05:00 EDT or Fri 2028-06-01 11:00 BST.

Best,
Mateo
--
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the quick reply. A few clarifications inline.

> For the batch 1k+ token jobs, are those acceptable to schedule on lower-priority nodes or must they be real-time?
They can be scheduled as lower-priority batch jobs — not latency-sensitive.

> Do you expect simultaneous long-running streams or mostly single-turn calls?
Mostly single-turn calls. We will have occasional multi-turn sessions but they are short (2–4 turns).

> Preferred KMS provider in the UK?
We are flexible; our security team prefers AWS KMS (London), but we can evaluate alternatives if Redwood recommends a better in-region option.

We can do the Thu 10:00 BST slot — Tom and I are available. We'll need the SOW and the cost ranges before procurement can sign off, but the timeline target (start week of 2028-08-05) stands.

Best,
Priya
